assign.request: The owner reloaded /framework/ai/ and got an error page. Find the likely cause of Servex's 0xC0000409 crash (or rule things out and add logging that would catch it), and make a Servex restart or crash invisible to the owner — proven by restarting Servex while a headless browser loads the page in a loop, with zero error pages.
assign.now: reading the logs around the 22:09:34 UTC crash
steps: read the logs around the crash
find or rule out the cause
add crash reports to the keeper
make the proxy ride out a restart
prove it: restart under a page-load loop

log.msg: Cause search: Servex died with 0xC0000409 three times — 2026-09-23 20:05:58 and 20:12:15 UTC, and today 22:09:34 UTC. Two of the three came within a second of a page load through the proxy; the first came 47 s after the last logged activity. Servex loads no native module (no .node file anywhere in its tree), so the fail-fast is inside node 24 itself. Windows recorded nothing: no Application Error event, no WER report, no LocalDumps key for node.exe, and stderr (sustain.log) got no 'Assertion failed' or 'FATAL ERROR' line. Not provable from what was kept.

decision.chose: A tiny detached 'gate' process owns port 80 and forwards raw TCP to Servex's proxy on an internal port, holding each connection and retrying until Servex answers; the proxy also waits for a just-restarted dev server instead of serving the Starting page. Crash reports turned on from inside Servex (process.report), so they deploy with a plain --restart.
decision.over: Putting the forwarder in the keeper (needs a keeper restart, which kills every running agent); a service worker in the site (adds caching machinery to every page); an auto-reloading error page (impossible — when nothing listens on port 80, Chrome draws its own error page).

assign.now: a minion builds the gate in worktree/servex-crash

agent.task: build the port-80 gate, the proxy retry and crash reports in worktree/servex-crash, and prove zero error pages across repeated Servex kills
build the port-80 gate, the proxy retry and crash reports in worktree/servex-crash, and prove zero error pages across repeated Servex kills
agent.outcome: committed c123de09; proof: 101 loads through the gate while a stand-in Servex (the real ReverseProxy plus a dev server as its child) was tree-killed 8 times gave 0 error pages, worst load 6.3 s; the same loop without the gate gave 23 and 4 error pages in two runs, worst a 30 s hang. The stand-in never exited 0xC0000409 on its own.

log.msg: Owner's system engineer asked who keeps the gate alive. Answer: Servex — it launches the gate at boot and relaunches it if port 80 stops answering (check tightened from 30 s to 5 s); the keeper keeps Servex; the logon Scheduled Task starts the keeper. Readme's 'Surviving a reboot' now says so. A page-side retry cannot replace the gate: when nothing listens on port 80, a reload never reaches the page's code, and Chrome draws its own error page.

assign.now: minion tightening the gate check and the reboot note; then merge and wait for a quiet moment to restart

assign.outcome:
**A Servex restart or crash now shows a slow page, not an error page.**

The cause of the crash was not found. Servex has died this way three times (twice on 2026-09-23, once today). Servex loads no native add-on, Windows kept no crash record, and nothing was written to the log, so the failure is inside node 24 itself. A test that tree-killed Servex eight times under constant page reloads did not trigger it. From now on, node writes a crash report to `%LOCALAPPDATA%/lew42/servex/logs/reports/`, so the next crash will leave a trace.

What happens during a restart now: a small separate process called the gate (`Servex/gate.mjs`) holds port 80. It passes each visitor on to Servex's proxy, which now listens on port 8079, and holds the connection until Servex answers again. The proxy also waits up to 15 s for the dev server to come back, instead of showing the "Starting…" page. Servex keeps the gate alive: it launches the gate at boot and checks it every 5 s. The keeper keeps Servex alive, and the logon Scheduled Task starts the keeper after a reboot.

The proof: 101 page loads while a stand-in Servex was killed 8 times gave 0 error pages, and the slowest load took 6.3 s. The same test without the gate gave 23 and then 4 error pages, with 30-second hangs.

log.msg: Regression found after the gate went live: sessions fail to connect to the site MCP with 'Unexpected content type: text/html'. At 18:18 the dev server answered POST /mcp directly, but about 1 in 6 POSTs through the proxy got the HTML Starting page. Cause (it predates the gate): ReverseProxy.failed() treats every proxy error as 'not running'. It calls autostart, which at 18:01 launched a second dev server that died with EADDRINUSE, and it answers any request with the HTML page. The GET-only retry never covered a POST. Fix in progress on worktree/servex-crash: POSTs and websockets wait for the port before proxying; only a refusal counts as 'not running'; other errors give a plain-text 502; non-navigations never get HTML; every proxy error is logged by code.

assign.now: fixing the proxy: an MCP POST got the HTML Starting page after a restart

decision.chose: Both fixes. (1) The proxy never answers a non-page request with HTML: it holds the request until the port answers, and otherwise sends a plain-text 503 or 502. (2) Dev servers outlive Servex: they are started detached with their output going to a file, re-adopted at boot by pid file and port, and stopped only when asked. After that, a Servex restart touches nothing the owner is looking at.
decision.over: (1) alone. It stops the HTML, but a module script that gets a 503 still fails to load, so the page still logs errors during every restart.

assign.now: minion: proxy fix, then dev servers that survive a Servex restart; proof = zero console errors reloading /framework/ai2/live/ across restarts

agent.task: proxy never answers non-page requests with HTML; dev servers survive a Servex restart (adopted by pid)
agent.outcome: Commits 951c1444, b362fe30, 7b9ee818. Proxy: 12 of 12 MCP POSTs made right after a kill ended as JSON 200 (never HTML); against a target resetting every 3rd connection, only plain-text 502s and no autostarts; 215 page loads across 7 kills with 0 error pages. Dev servers: 146 loads of /framework/ai2/live/ across 8 kills with 0 console errors, 0 failed requests and the same dev-server pid throughout, and its log lines kept flowing. Found: the proxy opened a fresh connection per request, and each waiting request checked the port itself about 400 times a second, which exhausted the machine's 16,384 outgoing ports (about 25,000 closed connections still held). The next connections failed with EADDRINUSE, which old code read as 'not running'. Fixed with keep-alive and one shared port check per project.

log.msg: Crash lead: during the port-exhaustion run, the stand-in Servex (only the proxy plus one child process) exited with 0xC0000409 on its own. It has not happened since the port fix. So running out of ports is a credible cause of the real Servex crashes, not proven; the crash reports now on will settle it.

Merged into michael/dev at 7b9ee818 under a hold; all Servex files parse; the merged tree booted on private ports (/api/system answered, the gate reached the dashboard); test processes killed. Goes live with the next Servex restart. That restart will be the last one to take the running dev server down with it, because that dev server was started under the old code.

assign.now: merged; asking restart_servex (it refuses while agents are mid-turn)
assign.outcome:
**A Servex restart is now invisible: the dev server keeps running, and nothing the owner is looking at reloads or errors.**

- **The gate** (`Servex/gate.mjs`) holds port 80 through any Servex restart or crash, so a reload waits instead of showing Chrome's error page.
- **Dev servers outlive Servex.** They start as their own hidden processes, and Servex re-adopts them at boot by pid file and port instead of restarting them. Their log lines keep flowing.
- **The proxy never answers a script, a fetch or an MCP call with an HTML page.** It waits for the port. Only a refused connection counts as 'not running'. Anything else gets a plain-text error, and every error is logged by code.
- **Proof:** 146 reloads of /framework/ai2/live/ across 8 Servex kills gave 0 console errors, with the same dev-server pid throughout. 12 of 12 MCP POSTs made right after a kill came back as JSON. The first gate test had given 0 error pages in 101 loads, against 23 without the gate.

**The crash (0xC0000409): likely cause found, not proven.** The proxy was exhausting the machine's outgoing ports: a new connection per request, plus about 400 port checks a second. In that state a stand-in Servex crashed with the same code on its own. Both are fixed, and node now writes a crash report to `%LOCALAPPDATA%/lew42/servex/logs/reports/` if it ever happens again.

Merged into michael/dev (7b9ee818, after 9bbb9839); live with the next Servex restart. Not tested: `sustain.mjs --stop` (it would have taken down every agent) and a boot of the real Servex (only private-port boots).
